title_es: Principios Well-Architected y pilar de confiabilidad
body_es: El AWS Well-Architected Framework es el conjunto de mejores prácticas de diseño de AWS organizado en seis pilares: Excelencia Operacional, Seguridad, Fiabilidad, Eficiencia de Rendimiento, Optimización de Costos, y Sostenibilidad. El Pilar de Fiabilidad (Reliability) es el más relevante para el SAA-C03 y se centra en la capacidad de un sistema para recuperarse de fallos e incorporar nueva demanda. Sus principios de diseño incluyen: recuperación automática de fallos, prueba de procedimientos de recuperación, escalar horizontalmente para aumentar disponibilidad agregada, no adivinar la capacidad y gestionar los cambios mediante automatización. Los fundamentos de fiabilidad en AWS son: límites de servicio (Service Quotas) que deben monitorizarse, planificación de redes (evitar solapamientos de CIDR), y gestión del cambio controlada. Los patrones de diseño para alta disponibilidad incluyen: Multi-AZ para instancias y bases de datos, multi-región para cargas globales críticas, circuit breakers para evitar fallos en cascada, y backoff exponencial con jitter para reintentos. El concepto de RTO (Recovery Time Objective) y RPO (Recovery Point Objective) define los requisitos de recuperación ante desastres. Las estrategias DR van de menor a mayor costo y velocidad: Backup and Restore, Pilot Light, Warm Standby y Multi-Site Active/Active.
body_en: The AWS Well-Architected Framework provides architectural best practices across six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability. The Reliability Pillar is most central to the SAA-C03 exam and defines a system's ability to recover from infrastructure or service disruptions and dynamically acquire computing resources to meet demand. Design principles include: automatically recovering from failure (CloudWatch alarms triggering Auto Scaling or failover), testing recovery procedures in practice, scaling horizontally to increase aggregate availability, stopping guessing capacity with elasticity, and managing change through automation. Reliability foundations cover AWS Service Quotas (monitor and request increases proactively), network topology (non-overlapping CIDRs across VPCs for seamless peering), and change management via CloudFormation and CI/CD pipelines. High-availability design patterns: Multi-AZ deployments for synchronous replication within a region, multi-region architecture for globally distributed or compliance-driven workloads, circuit breakers to prevent cascading failures, and exponential backoff with jitter for retry logic. Recovery strategies are defined by RTO (Recovery Time Objective — acceptable downtime) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective — acceptable data loss): from cheapest/slowest (Backup and Restore) through Pilot Light and Warm Standby to most expensive/fastest (Multi-Site Active/Active with real-time data replication).
example_code:
# Enable Multi-AZ for RDS
aws rds modify-db-instance \
  --db-instance-identifier my-postgres \
  --multi-az \
  --apply-immediately

# Enable versioning on S3
aws s3api put-bucket-versioning \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled

# Create CloudWatch alarm
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm \
  --alarm-name high-cpu \
  --alarm-description "Alert when CPU is high" \
  --metric-name CPUUtilization \
  --namespace AWS/EC2 \
  --statistic Average \
  --period 300 \
  --threshold 70
